title: Basel Framework — NSF (Net Stable Funding Ratio)
sourceNote: Structured rendering of the BCBS consolidated Basel Framework, standard group NSF (Net Stable Funding Ratio, d335 lineage). Verbatim source: https://www.bis.org/basel_framework/standard/NSF.htm. Binds the bank via SARB Reg 26A and BA 326.

sections.heading: The NSFR requirement
sections.text: The Net Stable Funding Ratio promotes resilience over a longer time horizon by requiring a bank to fund its activities with sufficiently stable sources of funding on an ongoing basis.

subsections.text: A bank must maintain available stable funding (ASF) of at least 100% of its required stable funding (RSF) on an ongoing one-year basis. The ratio is the amount of available stable funding relative to the amount of required stable funding.

sections.heading: Available stable funding factors
sections.text: ASF is the portion of capital and liabilities expected to be reliable over the one-year horizon, determined by applying ASF factors to funding sources.

subsections.text: ASF factors are assigned by funding type: regulatory capital and other liabilities with residual maturity of one year or more receive a 100% factor; stable retail and small-business deposits with residual maturity under one year 95%; less-stable such deposits 90%; operational deposits and wholesale funding from non-financial corporates under one year 50%; and other liabilities under one year, including funding from financial institutions, 0%.

sections.heading: Required stable funding factors
sections.text: RSF measures the amount of stable funding a bank's assets and off-balance-sheet exposures require, determined by applying RSF factors by asset class and residual maturity.

subsections.text: RSF factors are assigned by asset class: Level 1 HQLA 5%; Level 2A HQLA 15%; Level 2B HQLA 50%; performing loans by residual maturity from 10% (under six months) up to 85% (over one year, including residential mortgages); and net derivative liabilities 100%.
